Indian Standard
METHODS FOR DETERMINATION OF WOOL FIBRE CONTENT OF RAW WOOL

(Revised)
0. FOREWOR D

0.1 This revised Indian Standard was adopted by the Indian Standards Institution on 13 March 1964, after the draft fmalized by the Textile Standards Sectional Committee had been approved by the Textile Division Council. 0.2 Raw wool, that is, wool as shorn from the sheep or wool which is pulled, limed or ginned and carded, contains varying amount of impurities like sand, grease, suint, vegetable matter, tags and dung. It is, therefore, purchased on the basis of either laboratory scoured yield Formulation of an Indian Standard for or clean wool fibr-e content. determining the laboratory scoured yield and clean wool fibre content of raw wool has, therefore, become necessary. It was pointed out that, 0.3 This standard was first published in 1959. wool, the value for clean wool yield obtained on for a given raw the basis of the method prescribed in this standard differed from those obtained by some of the laboratories abroad. The Committee, on examining this matter in great detail, found that such differences were due to the differences in the nomenclature and the definition of the term used to indicate the clean wool fibre content in raw wool; in the earlier edition the term `clean wool vield' was used The Committee, therefore, in the sense of clean wool fihre content. including and defining the terms decided to prepare this revision ` laboratory scoured yield' and `clean wool fibre content' explicitly. This opportunity has been taken to change the sampling procedure so as to recognize the drawing of samples only from press-packed bales. In this Further changes have been incorporated in respect of reagents. revision, the determination of vegetable matter content has been made obligatory irrespective of whether the wool under test purports to be and consequently reference to a ` burry wool' or ` non-burry wool' ` burry ' and G non-burry ' wool is omitted. 3

1. SCOPE 1.1 This standard prescribes methods fibre content ( see 2.1) and laboratory wool. 2. TERMINOLOGY 2.0 For
apply. 2.1 Clean Wool Fibre Content - The weight of wool fibres, free from vegetable matter, grease, dirt and other impurities and adjusted to the standard condition of 13.8 percent moisture content, 1*5 percent alcohol extractable matter content and 05 percent ash content, the latter two calculated on the basis of the oven-dry weight of the scoured specimen. 2.2 Laboratory Scoured Yield -The total weight of wool fibres and vegetable matter free from grease, dirt and other impurities and adjusted to the standard condition of 13.8 percent moisture content, 1.5 percent alcohol extractable matter content and 0.5 percent ash content, the 4 the purpose of this standard, the following definitions shall for determination of clean wool scoured yield ( see 2.2 ) of raw

IS:1349-t96ri latter two calculated specimen. on the basis of the oven-dry weight of the scoured

of raw wool drawn from one definite type 2.3 Lot - The quantity of package purporting to be of one definite colour and quality delivered to one buyer against one despatch note. 2.4 Vegetable Matter - Burrs,: seeds, twigs, leaves and grasses that may be present in the sample of raw wool. Vegetable matter does not include vegetable fibres or'tag material that may be present in the sample of raw wool.

3. SAMPLING 3.1 Sample to evaluate the laboratory scoured yield and clean wool fibre content of raw wool in a lot shaJ1 be selected so as to be representative of the lot.
3.2 Sample to evaluate the laboratory scoured yield and clean wool fibre content of raw wool in a lot, selected in compliance with an agreement between the buyer and the seller, shall be held to be representative of the lot. 3.3 If there is no agreed method of drawing a test sample, the number of bales to be -selected at random from the lot shall be as specified All the bales so selected shall, taken together, constitute the in Table I.

bulk sample.

of maintaining *an inside temperature

7.1 Take a sealed container. If its label indicates the original weight of the test specimen contained therein, take the test specimen out and note its original weight ( IV, ). If the label of the container does not indicate the weight of the specimen contained therein, weigh the sealed container, remove the test specimen out of it, fe-weigh the container, and from the difference between the two weighings, determine the original weight (W,) of the test specimen. Open out the specimen either by hand or by mechanical means andfree it from impurities like dirt, dung, strings, etc, avoiding any loss of fibre and vegetable matter. Heat the scouring solu ion to 52" f 5�C and fill three tubs with it. Ratio. of wool weight, i o volume of solution used for scouring bath shall be less than 15 g per litre. Agitate the specimen ( enclosed in a 40 mesh net bag) in the basket for 3 to 5 minutes with hands. Use rubber gloves (alkali proof) for agitation. Remove the mesh bag with the specimen and squeeze between the rollers of wringers before it is passed on to the next tub. Treat the specimen ( see Note) similarly in the second and third tub. Fill rhe fourth tub 7

1964

with soft water and heat to 52" f 5�C and rinse the specimen in it. Remove the specimen and spray it with a strong stream of warm water so as to flush out, as much as possible, sand and other soil, pass the specimen through the rollers of wringers and centrifuge for five minutes to remove the excess of water. Dry the specimen in drying oven Note the oven-dry weight (W,) of the at 105" f 2�C to constant weight. Preserve the oven-dry specimen. specimen accur'ately.
NOTE - After scouring in each bowl, recover the fibre lost during scouring by floatation and add the recovered fibres to the origirial sample before drying.

7.2.1 Take about 10 g of scoured oven-dry specimen ( see 7.1). Re-dry it in a drying oven at 105"&t2"C, cool in a desiccator and weigh. Extract it with neutral alcohol in a Soxhlet extractor by heating on a water-bath Cool and disconnect the extraction flask. Recover for 20 extractions. bulk of the alcohol by distillation and evaporate the residue to. dryness by drying it to constant weight in the drying oven at 105" f 2�C.
